widgets_values:
subject_definitions:

<Subject 1> is the replacement character defined by <Picture 1>.
Preserve the complete visual identity of <Subject 1>, including facial identity,
facial proportions, hairstyle, hair accessories, body proportions, clothing,
colors, materials, surface details, and all distinctive appearance features.

<Picture 1> is the visual identity reference for <Subject 1>.
If multiple views of the same character are present, use all views together to
maintain consistent front, profile, three-quarter, and rear appearance.

<Video 1> is a hybrid structural editing reference.

The normal RGB regions of <Video 1> define the source scene that must be preserved,
including the environment, background, other people, props, camera position,
framing, lens behavior, camera movement, lighting, spatial layout, and temporal structure.

The grayscale depth-rendered region inside <Video 1> corresponds exclusively to
the tracked subject that must be replaced by <Subject 1>.

The depth-rendered region is not visual appearance.
Do not reproduce its grayscale color, shading, texture, or depth-map appearance
in the final video.

Use the depth-rendered region only as structural and motion guidance for:
body position,
silhouette,
3D volume,
body orientation,
pose,
limb trajectory,
limb depth ordering,
head movement,
torso movement,
gesture timing,
spatial position,
and temporal motion.

summary:

[character replacement + depth-guided motion reconstruction + source scene preservation]

Replace only the depth-rendered tracked subject in <Video 1> with <Subject 1>
from <Picture 1>.

Reconstruct <Subject 1> inside the depth-defined region while following the
depth region's body position, pose, silhouette, volume, motion trajectory,
spatial relationship, and timing.

Preserve all normal RGB regions of <Video 1> as strongly as possible.
Do not modify the environment, background, other people, props, camera behavior,
composition, lighting, or shot timing unless explicitly requested.

The replacement character must retain the identity, face, hairstyle, clothing,
colors, materials, and distinctive design defined by <Picture 1> throughout
the entire video.

The grayscale depth representation must completely disappear in the final result
and be replaced by the fully rendered appearance of <Subject 1>.

No residual original subject identity,
no original face,
no original clothing,
no grayscale depth texture,
no depth-map shading,
no hybrid anatomy,
no duplicated limbs,
no character morphing,
no unintended modification of other people,
no new subjects,
no new props,
no new camera movement,
and no unintended scene changes.

nodes.title: Switches
widgets_values:
⬆️ **Mode**: Role Swap replaces the person. Fashion is the optional native H3 branch.
⬆️ **Face refine**: Adaptive = best detail and identity (recommended).
###### The switches write into the controls node below.
⬆️ **Precise face mask (SAM3)**: the Adaptive refine re-renders and pastes only the face SAM3 finds (sharper eyes and mouth, hair untouched). Needs the SAM3.1 model; off = elliptical area.
⬆️ **Character swap LoRA v1.5**: akatz-ai LoRA after the Pika adapter, for a face closer to Picture 1 (tested: identity +5-12%). It can open the smile like Picture 1; lower its strength (03F) if the expression looks forced.

{"v": 1, "title": "LAu Motion Transfer · Guide + models", "subtitle": "Replace the person in a dance or motion clip with your character. The moves, the camera and the sound stay.", "author": "LAu", "layout": "card", "accent": "", "body": "1. Load your clip in **Source video** and your person in **Picture 1** (a clear face close-up).
2. Optional but recommended: a **full-body photo** in **Picture 2**, then switch on *Use the character sheet* in Settings → Extras. Without it H3 invents the clothes, legs and shoes from the original dancer.
3. In the **Points Editor** Shift+Click the body of the person to replace on frame 0 (the first frame of the chosen part; after changing Start, run once so the editor shows the new frame).
4. Set the **purple** settings: Start + Duration (the part of the clip to copy), Seed, Target resolution (1.0 MP).
5. **Face refine = Adaptive** for the best face. Queue.

**First run:** switch on *Save debug files* once and open **Debug_RGB_Depth**: the whole person must be grey. If the original person survives, the points are on the background.

**Run times** (RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB, 128 GB RAM): 10 s at 1.0 MP ≈ 32 min + face refine. 15 s ≈ 2 h (VRAM overflow). For 20 s, make two 10 s clips.

**Custom node:** `ComfyUI-KoO-Motion-Control` ships with this workflow: copy the folder to `ComfyUI/custom_nodes/`. ComfyUI-H3-FaceRefine must be **1.1.2 or newer** (older versions fail with *tuple index out of range*).

Optional upscalers and which one to use for fast or slow motion: open the **Upscale guide** tile below.

Face refine · Adaptive | what happens here
widgets_values: Recommended face refine. Base frames → model upscale (2x) → resize to 1.5x → identity face tracking (InsightFace + YOLO) → 1024 × 1024 face crops → H3 Ref2VA re-render with Picture 1 → face size fade (full fix on small faces, none on close-ups) → SAM3 face mask, so only the face is re-rendered (switch 'Precise face mask') → per-frame denoise (0.35) → stitch back along the SAM3 face outline (ellipse when the switch is off). Use canvas 768/896 for long clips. Denoise above ~0.45 lets the head drift from the neck. InsightFace weights are non-commercial by default.

widgets_values_named.text: Recommended face refine. Base frames → model upscale (2x) → resize to 1.5x → identity face tracking (InsightFace + YOLO) → 1024 × 1024 face crops → H3 Ref2VA re-render with Picture 1 and the realism LoRAs (prompt starts with “r34l1sm, Facial Realism.”) → per-frame denoise (0.35) → ellipse stitch back. Canvas 1024 is needed for the LoRAs to show; use 768/896 for long clips. Denoise above ~0.45 lets the head drift from the neck. InsightFace weights are non-commercial by default.
